newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola president said being pressed to meet Savimbi.
newsitem.headline: Angola president said being pressed to meet Savimbi.

text.p: Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos faces increasing foreign pressure to meet former rebel leader Jonas Savimbi to discuss ongoing fighting in the country's diamond-rich northeast, intelligence sources said on Thursday.
The president had promised foreign governments, including the United States and Portugal, he would contact Savimbi on his return from a three-week holiday in Sardinia, Italy, one source told Reuters.
Dos Santos arrived home on Wednesday night and analysts said they expected him to telephone Savimbi at UNITA's new headquarters at Andulo on Friday, at the earliest.
"The only way to prevent another costly round of fighting is another meeting and an understanding between President dos Santos and Dr Savimbi," one analyst told Reuters.
In response to an appeal from U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, UNITA said Savimbi was ready to meet Dos Santos in Italy, but the Luanda government insists any talks take place in Angola.
Previous discussions between the two rivals have been in neighbouring countries, mainly because of Savimbi's security worries.
The Angolan government launched an offensive in the northeast of the country last month, saying it wanted to drive out armed refugees crossing from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
But analysts say that was a pretext for an assault on UNITA, which still controls the main diamond-producing areas in the region.
Observers and diplomats fear heavy fighting between the parties threatens a ceasefire signed in 1994 to end 20 years of conflict.
The government offensive coincided with the fall last month of Mobutu Sese Seko, the former Zairean president who backed the UNITA rebels.
The government and UNITA joined a power-sharing government in April, but Savimbi has refused to come to the capital Luanda and vast areas of the country as still under UNITA control.
Diplomats said they believed a meeting between Dos Santos and Savimbi would take place after a national conference of the ruling MPLA scheduled for July 1 to 5.
